title: Add subroutine Predefined_Int_SaSb
Analysis: the jackknife error estimates across the ALF codebase assume (N - 1) / N ≈ 1
body:
In principle I have the same question for pyALF, but posting here since I have checked that the equivalent [pyALF analysis function](https://github.com/ALF-QMC/pyALF/blob/16d706111eceba6687c6d301389c94cc3c3bace6/py_alf/ana.py#L171-L194) is a transliteration of its ALF counterpart(s).

# Error calculation in ALF

Consider the jackknife bins

$$\text{Bin}_i = \frac{1}{N-1}\sum_{\substack{j=1 \\ j\neq i}}^{N} x_j, \quad i=1,\dots,N$$

and a function

$$\theta_i = f(\text{Bin}_i).$$

The mean of this function is

$$\bar\theta = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\theta_i$$

and the jackknife variance estimator on the mean is

$$V = \frac{N-1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}(\theta_i-\bar\theta)^2$$

yielding the standard error of the function mean as $$SE=\sqrt{V}$$.

The above typical definition of a jackknife variance estimator is exactly what the ALF documentation quotes
https://github.com/ALF-QMC/ALF/blob/e43e087e1a319ef6aada91f8ba3ae57385488496/Documentation/sampling.tex#L58-L64
but this is *not* what is computed in ALF. In fact it seems that the version of this formula actually implemented across ALF and pyALF effectively assumes the variance factor

$$\frac{N - 1}{N} \approx 1.$$

For calculations thus far this is effectively over-estimating the error, but obviously with large $N$ there is very little difference between $(N-1)/N$ and $1$.

# Exposure

Across ALF and pyALF there are three general places where this calculation occurs and I have checked they all match between themselves:

1. The subroutine `jack` in `Analysis/ana_mod.F90` simply takes the standard deviation of the jackknife bins and returns this as the error: https://github.com/ALF-QMC/ALF/blob/e43e087e1a319ef6aada91f8ba3ae57385488496/Analysis/ana_mod.F90#L913-L929.

2. The `ERRCALC_J*` family of subroutines in `Libraries/Modules/errors_mod.F90` does the same, for instance: https://github.com/ALF-QMC/ALF/blob/e43e087e1a319ef6aada91f8ba3ae57385488496/Libraries/Modules/errors_mod.F90#L329-L388.

3. pyALF does the same [here](https://github.com/ALF-QMC/pyALF/blob/16d706111eceba6687c6d301389c94cc3c3bace6/py_alf/ana.py#L171-L194).

# Question

I am curious, is this a deliberate choice of approximation? I couldn't find a note in the source code or the documentation resolving this.

# Additional issue

It's worth mentioning that the subroutine `jack` in `Analysis/ana_mod.F90` is not called by default in ALF; the code currently is calling `ERRCALC_J*` for jackknife calculations, e.g. in sign-reweighting, and has the `_F` variant for an arbitrary function. This seems like a multiple-sources of truth issue; it may be advantageous to trim the dead code.

title: Add configure.fish, a wrapper of configure.sh for fish shell.
body:
Adds a Fish shell wrapper around `configure.sh` so Fish users can set up the ALF build environment by sourcing a Fish script, while still reusing the existing POSIX `configure.sh` logic.

## Changes

- Introduces `configure.fish` to invoke `configure.sh` in a POSIX `sh` subshell, using portable `mktemp` fallback for BSD/macOS compatibility.
- Passes paths as positional parameters to `sh -c` to correctly handle spaces and special characters.
- Captures the resulting environment and imports `ALF_*` variables into the current Fish session.
- Guards against incorrect usage: errors with a clear message if the script is not sourced inside an interactive Fish shell session (e.g. executed directly or sourced from bash/sh).

## Usage

```fish
source configure.fish MACHINE [MODE] [STAB] [options]
# or
. configure.fish MACHINE [MODE] [STAB] [options]
```

See `configure.sh` for the full list of `MACHINE`, `MODE`, `STAB`, and option values.

```Fortran

```
But [this line](https://github.com/ALF-QMC/ALF/blob/3af8e24de50e9b8ef479fc9df3336261b1b17e3b/Libraries/Modules/maxent_mod.F90#L199) labels it as "1/Alpha".
```Fortran
2006       FORMAT('Res: 1/Alpha, XQ,S,CHI: ', E25.17E3,2x,E25.17E3,2x,E25.17E3,2x,E25.17E3)
```

Similarly, there is also [this line](https://github.com/ALF-QMC/ALF/blob/master/Libraries/Modules/maxent_mod.F90#L162):
```Fortran
               WRITE(44,*)  '========= 1/Alpha:    ', ALPHA
```

Notably, Conversely, `Subroutine MaxEnt_T_Bryan` in the same file is consistent: It writes alpha, labeled as alpha.

title: 627 ci pginvhpc runtime crash illegal instruction exit code 132 when executing progalfout
body:
When compiling HDF5 with nvfortran, it defaults to hardware-dependant optimization flags (namely `-fast`), which can cause errors with e.g. the pre-compiled HDF5 binaries shipped with the images from https://github.com/ALF-QMC/alf-container. This pull request solves this by setting the optimization to -O3 in `HDF5/install_hdf5.sh`.

This pull request also updates HDF5 patch version from 1.14.5 to 1.14.6 and gives the workflow `test-broad.yml` a better concurrency group name.

title: Fix PGI/NVHPC CI crash: replace -fast with -tp=px, remove -Mfprelaxed, fix link step target, guard OMP thread count, and build HDF5 with portable flags
body:
PGI/NVHPC CI jobs crash with exit code 132 (Illegal instruction) due to five related issues:

1. `-fast` implies `-tp=native`, generating host-tuned (znver3) instructions that Intel GitHub-hosted runners don't support.
2. `-Mfprelaxed` enables `-Mfma` (FMA3 instructions) and `-Mfpapprox` (approximate floating-point operations) which can conflict with the `-tp=px` (SSE2-only) target in NVHPC 24.x, causing the compiler to emit non-portable instructions even with `-tp=px` set.
3. The Makefile link steps called `$(ALF_FC)` without any target flags. NVHPC at link time defaulted to its installed target (`znver3`) when selecting runtime libraries (`libpgmath`, OpenMP runtime, etc.), which contain znver3-specific instructions (VAES, VPCLMULQDQ, SHA-NI) not supported on Intel GitHub-hosted runners.
4. The NVHPC OpenMP runtime's worker-thread creation code contains Zen3-specific instructions. When `OMP_NUM_THREADS` is unset the runtime tries to use all available CPUs and spawns worker threads that execute this Zen3 code. The analysis programs already guarded against this by calling `check_omp_num_threads()` at startup, but `main.F90` was missing this call.
5. When HDF5 is built inside container images using NVHPC without explicit target flags, NVHPC defaults to `-tp=native` (= `-tp=znver3` on the container build machine), embedding Zen3-specific instructions into the HDF5 static libraries (`libhdf5*.a`). Those instructions crash with SIGILL on Intel GitHub-hosted runners.

## Changes

- **`configure.sh`**: Replace `-fast` with `-tp=px` and remove `-Mfprelaxed` from `PGIOPTFLAGS` to target the portable x86_64 baseline without non-SSE2 floating-point extensions. Add `ALF_FLAGS_LINK="-tp=px -mp"` in the PGI compiler section only — minimal link-only flags so NVHPC selects the portable `px` variant of its runtime libraries. This is intentionally **not** derived from `F90OPTFLAGS` (which contains compiler-specific flags such as `-static` for Intel that must not appear at link time).

```sh
# Before
PGIOPTFLAGS="-Mpreprocess -O3 -Mfprelaxed -fast"

# After
PGIOPTFLAGS="-Mpreprocess -O3 -tp=px"
# (plus ALF_FLAGS_LINK="-tp=px -mp" for the link step)
```

- **`Prog/Makefile`**: Pass `$(ALF_FLAGS_LINK)` to the `ALF.out` link step so NVHPC selects the portable `px` variant of its runtime libraries instead of the default `znver3` variant. For non-PGI compilers `ALF_FLAGS_LINK` is unset and expands to nothing.

- **`Analysis/Makefile`**: Same fix for the analysis tool link step.

- **`testsuite/CMakeLists.txt`**: Honour `ALF_FLAGS_LINK` via `add_link_options` (guarded by `if(DEFINED ENV{ALF_FLAGS_LINK})`) so cmake-built unit test binaries also use portable runtime libraries.

- **`Prog/main.F90`**: Add `use check_omp_num_threads_mod` and `call check_omp_num_threads()` (both guarded by `#ifdef _OPENMP`) right after `MPI_Init` and before any OpenMP parallel regions. When `OMP_NUM_THREADS` is unset this limits each process to 1 OMP thread — matching the existing behaviour of all analysis programs — and prevents the NVHPC OpenMP runtime from spawning multi-threaded worker teams that contain Zen3-specific thread-initialisation code.

- **`HDF5/install_hdf5.sh`**: Detect PGI/NVHPC via `$FC --version` and, when detected, set `CFLAGS`/`CXXFLAGS`/`FCFLAGS="-O2 -tp=px"` before calling HDF5's `configure` script. This ensures the resulting `libhdf5*.a` static libraries contain only portable SSE2 baseline code rather than hardware-tuned Zen3 instructions. The `${VAR:=value}` idiom is used so any user-provided flags take precedence. This fix takes effect for local builds and when the `alf-container` images are rebuilt.

title: CI (PGI/NVHPC) runtime crash: Illegal instruction (exit code 132) when executing Prog/ALF.out
body:
The PGI/NVHPC Linux CI job builds Prog/ALF.out successfully, but the test run crashes immediately with an illegal instruction (exit code 132). This usually indicates an ISA/CPU-feature mismatch (e.g., binaries compiled with instructions not supported by the GitHub-hosted runner CPU), potentially due to compiler target flags (like -tp=native / host-tuned -fast) or linked libraries built for a newer microarchitecture.

Evidence
Failing job (example):

Workflow run/job (PR context, but treated as a general CI issue):
https://github.com/ALF-QMC/ALF/actions/runs/23872788788/job/69608890799?pr=626
Log excerpt:

Text
pgfortran -o "ALF.out" ...
... Illegal instruction (core dumped) "$ALF_DIR/Prog/ALF.out"
Process completed with exit code 132.
Expected behavior
Prog/ALF.out should run successfully in the PGI/NVHPC CI environment.

Suggested mitigation (first step)
For PGI/NVHPC CI builds, compile for a portable x86_64 baseline rather than “native” CPU tuning:

avoid -tp=native (and consider avoiding -fast if it implies host tuning in this setup)
explicitly set something like: -tp=px (portable x86)
This should prevent generating instructions not supported by the runner CPU.

title: Remove unused variables, fix compiler warnings, and standardize constants for -pedantic builds
body:
Using the `-pedantic` and `-Wunused-variable` flags, various compiler warnings were cleaned up across the codebase.

**Unused variables and imports:**
- Removed unused local variables across 30+ Fortran modules and programs.
- Moved MPI/HDF5-only locals (e.g., `ierr`, loop indices) behind `#ifdef _MPI` / `#ifdef _HDF5` preprocessor guards to avoid warnings in non-MPI/HDF5 builds.
- Removed unused imports of `pi` from `Natural_Constants` in files where only `twopi` is actually referenced.

**Standardized mathematical and numerical constants:**
- Extended the `Natural_Constants` module with `pi = acos(-1.d0)`, `twopi`, `Eps_machine = 1.D-12`, `Eps_small = 1.D-10`, and `Eps_convergence = 1.D-6` as a single source of truth.
- Replaced all local hardcoded definitions of `pi` and small tolerance values (e.g., `1.D-10`, `1.D-8`) across the codebase with imports from `Natural_Constants`.

**Other fixes:**
- Changed `INTENT(IN), target` to `INTENT(INOUT), target` for dummy arguments whose addresses are stored in pointers in `observables_mod` and `DynamicMatrixArray_mod`, as required by flang. Added inline comments and updated Doxygen `@param` tags explaining the rationale.
- Fixed spelling in `udv_state_mod.F90` warning message: "smalles" → "smallest representable value".

The `libqrref` files with non-standard `complex*16` declarations were intentionally left unchanged.

title: 623 enhance safety
body:
Adds a centralized safety/validation layer to ensure Hamiltonian-global variables and core arrays are initialized and correctly set by each `Ham_Set`, preventing undefined/uninitialized state from propagating into the Monte Carlo core.

## Changes Made

- Initialize key Hamiltonian globals (`Ndim`, `N_FL`, `N_SUN`, `Ltrot`, `Thtrot`, `Projector`, `Symm`) to sentinel/safe defaults in `Alloc_Ham`.
- Validate required Hamiltonian globals and allocations right after `ham%Ham_set()` (including `Op_V`, `Op_T`, and projector trial wavefunctions).
- Ensure `Thtrot` is explicitly initialized in relevant `Ham_Set` implementations.
- Add Hermiticity check in `Op_set` to validate operator matrices, merging Hermiticity and diagonal-detection into a single O(N²) upper-triangle pass.
- Add `Op_equal` function in `Operator_mod` to compare two `Operator` instances on their defining properties (used for structural checks).
- Add `Op_V_is_symmetric` function in `Operator_mod` that verifies the product `(I+g₁V₁)···(I+gₙVₙ)` equals its reverse — satisfied by palindromic arrangement or mutually commuting operators.
- Validate that all projector indices `P(i)` in `Op_V` and `Op_T` are within `[1, Ndim]` in `Validate_Ham_Variables`, preventing out-of-bounds memory access before any matrix indexing occurs.
- Validate that the `Op_V` operator sequence is symmetric when `Symm = .true.`, terminating with a clear error if not.
- Add `iso_fortran_env` import for `error_unit` in `Operator_mod`.
- Add test suite coverage for `Op_set` validation (tests 28–32), including Hermiticity failure, type failure, projector index failure, and 1×1 matrix failure.
- Add test suite coverage for `Op_equal` and `Op_V_is_symmetric` (tests 33–35): operator equality comparison, symmetric `Op_V` pass, and asymmetric `Op_V` fail.

title: Enhance safety
body:
We should enhance the safety with regard to some critical parameter choices, model implementations.

Currently, there are some variables that are essential, such as N_SUN, that get declared in Hamiltonian_main and should be initialised or set by the Hamiltonian of a given model. If a model misses this, random values could get used, e.g., N_SUN=0. This is an unphysical setting and surprisingly hard to detect.

While we are at it, we should enhance our consistency and correctness check. E.g., we rely on hermitian operators when they are diagonalised but never check this property.

title: Upgrade for input of parallel params.
body:
Parallel params is a nice way of launching simulations for several parameters at once.
The core feature works perfectly fine, however from a user perspective it is not well documented how to use the feature/correctly setup the simulation directories.

It seems like people who use the feature rely on some internal scripts to setup the simulation.
I am working on a script, that uses the existing parameters file in combination with some new convention, in order to automatically generate the Temp folders and individual parameter files. 
On top of that it creates links (ln -s "Temp_i" "some-human-readable-format-containing-infos-about-parameters"), so that the Temp folders become easier to differentiate.



**Explanation of the notation:**
_Example 1:
&VAR_lattice             
L1           = {4, 6, 8}            
L2           = 0         
Lattice_type = "Square"     
Model        = "Hubbard"   
/
..._

This creates three simulations of a 1D chain, with sizes 4, 6, 8.

_Example 2:
&VAR_lattice             
L1           = {4, 6, 8}            
L2           = {4, 6, 8}              
Lattice_type = "Square"     
Model        = "Hubbard"   
/
..._

This creates 3*3 simulations of a 2D lattice, with sizes (L1 =4, L2 = 4), (L1=4, L2=6)...

_Example 3:
&VAR_lattice             
L1           = {4, 6, 8}            
L2           = [4, 6, 8; VAR_lattice, L1]             
Lattice_type = "Square"     
Model        = "Hubbard"   
/
..._

This creates 3 simulations of a 2D lattice with sizes (L1=4, L2=4) (L1=6, L2=6), (L1=8, L2=8).
Notice that the square brackets link the L2 list with the "L1" element in the namelist "VAR_lattice".

_Example 4:
&VAR_lattice             
L1           = {4, 6, 8}            
L2           = [6, 1, 3; VAR_lattice, L1]             
Lattice_type = "Square"     
Model        = "Hubbard"   
/
..._

This creates 3 simulations of a 2D lattice with sizes (L1=4, L2=6) (L1=6, L2=1), (L1=8, L2=3).


**Some advanced examples:**

This is an example of a parameter file, how it is would be used with the new script.
[parameters_easy.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26245863/parameters_easy.txt)
Some cleaned up version, in order to see the applications better:
[parameters_easy_cleaned.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26245971/parameters_easy_cleaned.txt)

Explanation:
With this parameter file, one would set up a **u sweep** for different **square lattice sizes**.  A **pi-flux** square lattice per plaquette is used, thus for each lattice size N_phi needs to be set to N_Phi = L1*L2/2. 
This is done using the convention from example 4: N_Phi        = [8, 18, 32; VAR_lattice, L1]  
The pi-flux generates Dirac fermions, therefore we would like to use \beta=L scaling, which is again done like in example 4: Beta         = [4, 6, 8; VAR_lattice, L1].


**But we can go even further and use this for Benchmarking, etc.:**
All Namelists (except &VAR_errors, &VAR_Max_Stoch) and all types, i.e. booleans, integers, floats are supported.

Full parameter files, how it would be used:
[parameters.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26246508/parameters.txt)

Cleaned up for readability:
[parameters copy.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26246578/parameters.copy.txt)

This would launch U sweeps for the for the Hubbard model and the tV model.
For different square lattices.

It would test the effects of Checkerboard and Symm. (E.g. for debugging...)
We again use the pi-flux square lattice (Thus N_phi=L_1*L_2/2) and again \beta=L scaling.
Also for some reason different Nwrap are probed in this example.


While this last example might not be useful in its application, it shows nicely, what is possible when establishing such a notation. 
I am currently already writing the script, in order to enable this.

Fix Compute_Ratio_Global call sites for log-scale signature change
body:
`Compute_Ratio_Global` signature changed to accept `log_T0_proposal_ratio` but two call sites (Langevin HMC and parallel tempering) were not updated.

## Changes

**Prog/Langevin_HMC_mod.F90**
- Variable: `T0_Proposal_ratio` → `log_T0_Proposal_ratio`
- Value: `1.0` → `0.0d0`
- Function call updated to pass log value

**Prog/Global_mod.F90 (Exchange_Step)**
- Variable: `T0_Proposal_ratio` → `log_T0_Proposal_ratio`  
- Value: `1.d0` → `0.d0`
- Function call updated to pass log value

```fortran
! Before (causes type mismatch)
T0_Proposal_ratio = 1.0
Ratiotot = Compute_Ratio_Global(..., T0_Proposal_ratio, ...)

! After (log scale)
log_T0_Proposal_ratio = 0.0d0  ! log(1.0) = 0
Ratiotot = Compute_Ratio_Global(..., log_T0_Proposal_ratio, ...)
```

All three call sites in the codebase now use the log-scale interface consistently.

title: Fix code review issues: missing imports, duplicate lock, and MPI file I/O
body:
Addresses code review feedback on PR #566 (QMC runtime variables implementation).

## Changes

- **Added module-level imports**: `output_unit` and `error_unit` from `iso_fortran_env` in `QMC_runtime_var_mod.F90` to fix compilation errors where symbols were used without import

- **Removed duplicate lock**: Eliminated redundant `lock_QMC_runtime_settings()` call in `main.F90:485` since it's already called inside `check_update_schemes_compatibility():234`

- **Fixed MPI file I/O**: Wrapped file operations in `read_and_broadcast_TEMPERING_var()` with rank 0 check to prevent multiple processes from reading the same file

```fortran
CALL MPI_COMM_RANK(MPI_COMM_WORLD, irank, ierr)
IF (irank == 0) THEN
  OPEN(UNIT=5,FILE='parameters',STATUS='old',ACTION='read',IOSTAT=ierr)
  ! ... read and close ...
END IF
CALL MPI_BCAST(...)  ! Broadcast to all ranks
```

- **Minor fixes**: Corrected spelling ("Bradcast" → "Broadcast") and indentation in error handling

title: WS construction in Make_lattice may generate wrong number of real-space points near boundaries
body:
***In GitLab by @pangaopei on Jan 22, 2026, 02:31 UTC:***

Recently, Disha encountered a problem very similar to what I reported before in issue #294.

When the lattice type is triangular, honeycomb, or kagome, the subroutine
```
Libraries/Modules/lattices_v3_mod.F90
  subroutine Make_lattice
```
(approximately lines 176–240)

uses a Wigner–Seitz (WS) construction to generate the real-space lattice. However, in many cases, this procedure does not correctly handle points on or near the boundary of the WS cell, which leads to an incorrect number of lattice points being generated.

In particular, the number of generated points can be larger than the expected L1*L2.

**Example**

Using the following input:
```
&VAR_lattice               !! Parameters defining the specific lattice and base model 
  L1           = 10            ! Length in direction a_1
  L2           = 4             ! Length in direction a_2
  Lattice_type = "triangular"  ! 
/
```
the code reports an error:
```
Make_lattice: Error           40          41
lattices_v3_mod.F90 (274):
Generic error
Terminating program
```
**Where the problem seems to come from**

The issue seems to originate from the WS construction  part in lines ~216–240 of `Libraries/Modules/lattices_v3_mod.F90`, namely:
```fortran
           nc = 0
           do i1 = -L,L
              do i2 = -L,L
                 x_p  = dble(i1)*a1_p + dble(i2)*a2_p
                 L_f = 1
                 do i = 1,4
                    if (i.eq.1) a_p =  L2_p
                    if (i.eq.2) a_p =  L1_p
                    if (i.eq.3) a_p =  L2_p - L1_p
                    if (i.eq.4) a_p =  L2_p + L1_p
                    if  (  Iscalar( x_p, a_p )    .le.  xnorm(a_p)**2/2.d0 + Zero   .and.   &
                         & Iscalar( x_p, a_p )    .ge. -xnorm(a_p)**2/2.d0 + Zero    ) then
                       L_f = L_f * 1
                    else
                       L_f = 0
                    endif
                 enddo
                 if (L_f .eq. 1) then
                    nc = nc + 1
                    Latt%list(nc,1) = i1
                    Latt%list(nc,2) = i2
                    Latt%invlist(i1, i2 ) = nc
                 endif
              enddo
           enddo
```
and also Line 256-257.

**More generally**

There are many combinations of (L1, L2) that trigger this problem (I have not exhaustively tested them, but a large fraction of combinations seem to fail).

For example, combinations like:
`(6,2),(8,2),(10,2)...(10,4),(12,4),(14,4)...(2,6)(14,6)(16,6)(18,6)...(2,8)(18,8)(20,8)...`
can also lead to wrong behavior.

(To Disha: I think your case is (20,8)? )

**Likely cause**

The current WS construction in `Make_lattice` seems to:

- Include boundary points in an inconsistent way
- Not treat floating-point tolerances (eps) carefully
- As a result, some boundary points are double-counted or incorrectly included

This leads to:

The number of generated real-space lattice points being larger than L1 * L2.

**Suggestion**

We probably need to:
- Revisit the WS-cell inclusion test
- And treat the epsilon tolerance in a more robust and consistent way to avoid double counting or missing of boundary points.

title: Missing safety checks for the number of field in confin (HDF5 version)
body:
***In GitLab by @pangaopei on Nov 14, 2025, 16:58 UTC:***

I found that in the HDF5-based workflow, there is no check for the number of `field` stored in `confin.h5`. This may lead to unsafe behavior when the dimensions of the fields do not match the values in `parameters` (e.g., `ltrot`).

Under normal case, a mismatch between `ltrot` in `parameters` and the field dimensions in `confin.h5` would be caught by the consistency checks against `data.h5`, and an error would be raised:
```
Error in test_attribute_double:
  Attribute name: "beta"
  Supplied value: 8.000000
  Read value:     6.000000
  Difference = 2.000000
 alf_hdf5_mod.F90 (757):
 Generic error
 Terminating program
1
```
then everything is OK. (Also suggests highlighting the difference comes from things in `data.h5` and in `parameters` in the error info. Sometimes, people will think `data.h5` only saves measurement, without parameters.)

However, in certain situations — for example, the case encountered by Disha — the user copied only `confout.h5` and `confin.h5` but not `data.h5`. When `parameters` contains an incorrect `ltrot` value (larger than the dimension in `confin.h5`), the program performs **out-of-bounds** array accesses while reading the fields. The run continues and later fails with errors such as `NaN` elements in the Green’s function, instead of stopping immediately with a clear message of the mismatch of dimension of fields:
```
 Warning: Smallest scale is approaching the smalles representable value.
          Consider switching to LOG.
```
or an error like:
```
Green function A contains NaN, calculation is being aborted!

 control_mod.F90 (239):
 Generic error
 Terminating program
```

**which is not clear what happened.**

This suggests that `Fields_mod.F90` lacks a necessary consistency check. In particular, after:
```
CALL h5dget_space_f(dset_id, dataspace, hdferr)

! Get dataspace's rank
CALL h5sget_simple_extent_ndims_f(dataspace, rank, hdferr)
```
there is no verification that the dimensions of fields in `confin.h5` match the allocated size of `this%f`.

Would it make sense to add an explicit check such as:
```
if (dims(1) /= SIZE(this%f,1) .or. dims(2) /= SIZE(this%f,2)) then
    STOP "ERROR: configuration size mismatch!"
endif
```
to prevent silent **out-of-bounds** access and provide a clear diagnostic early?

I would like to hear your thoughts on whether such a check should be added, or if you believe this situation should be handled in a different way or just ignore this.
